issue.title: Document that it is unsafe to call `curses.initscr` after `curses.setupterm`
issue.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

```python
import curses
import sys
import os

# Ensure TERM is set so setupterm doesn't fail
if not os.environ.get('TERM'):
    os.environ['TERM'] = 'xterm'

# 1. First allocation (from TestCurses.setUpClass)
# This allocates the first 'struct term' and assigns it to the global cur_term.
try:
    curses.setupterm(fd=sys.stdout.fileno())
except curses.error:
    # If setupterm fails (e.g. no terminal info), we can't reproduce the leak.
    sys.exit(0)

# 2. Second allocation (from TestCurses.setUp -> curses.initscr)
# initscr() internally calls newterm(), which allocates a NEW 'struct term'.
# This overwrites the global cur_term pointer, leaking the memory from step 1.
stdscr = curses.initscr()

# Cleanup (standard curses exit, though the leak has already happened)
curses.endwin()
```

comments.body:
Two possible solutions:

- Forbid initscr() after setupterm() though I need to check if curses allows me this restriction.
-  Find another way to deallocate the current terminal. The problem is that we do not know whether cur_term is being used elsewhere and this may be annoying. 

I will investigate when I am back home, that is, this week-end.

So I didn't have time to investigate. If someone wants to help here, we need a solution that is not deterimental and that could still work with the capsule API (my major concern). I don't know if forbidding initscr() after setupterm() makes sense (it would be the easiest approach...). Or just document that we shouldn't do it because we can't reliably find a way to deallocate the terminal.

Suggest documenting rather than fixing in code.

This is standard ncurses single-`cur_term` behaviour -- `initscr()`/`newterm()` allocates a new terminal and abandons the one `setupterm()` made; C leaks the same. `del_curterm()` isn't safe to call automatically (capsule API + live terminfo queries -- hence gh-144076 stalled), and forbidding the sequence would break our own test suite's `setUpClass`/`setUp` pattern. It's a one-time libtinfo leak, so a note on `setupterm()` should do:

> **Note:** Calling `initscr()` or `newterm()` after `setupterm()` leaks the terminal `setupterm()` allocated: the curses library keeps a single current terminal and does not free the previous one.

Opened #152624 to document this on `setupterm()` (cross-referenced from `initscr()`/`newterm()`).

A code fix isn't safe — freeing `cur_term` would break the capsule API and pending terminfo queries (cf. the closed #144076) — so a doc note is the right resolution for this one-time libtinfo leak.
